cases.purpose: --partx-kernel rejects a bad OP, non-numeric/negative/over-range bounds, MIN>MAX and a wrong operand count, and a uid 2000 caller is refused with 'BLKPG mutation requires uid 0' for add, delete and update before the device is opened.
cases.oracle: Documented fdisk --partx-kernel OP DEV [MIN MAX] contract from the candidate usage text (loadables/fdisk.c header) and util-linux partx argument rules; every case exits before any device is opened, so no kernel partition table is touched.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.
cases.script:
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/dev/null 2>err.txt; local rc=$? e c; e=$(< err.txt)
  case $e in *"OP must be"*) c=bad-op;; *"invalid minimum"*) c=bad-min;; *"invalid maximum"*) c=bad-max;; *"MIN is greater than MAX"*) c=min-gt-max;;
    *"requires uid 0"*) c=needs-uid0;; *"not a block device"*) c=not-block;; *"requires OP DEV"*) c=usage;; '') c=none;; *) c=other:$e;; esac
  printf '%s status=%s err=%s\n' "$l" $rc "$c"; }
r bad-op fdisk --partx-kernel frobnicate nodev
r bad-minimum fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev abc
r bad-maximum fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev 1 2x
r negative-bound fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev -1 2
r bound-over-int-max fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev 2147483648
r min-greater-than-max fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev 5 2
r no-device fdisk --partx-kernel add
r too-many-args fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev 1 2 3
r add-non-root fdisk --partx-kernel add nodev
r delete-non-root fdisk --partx-kernel delete nodev 1 4
r update-non-root fdisk --partx-kernel update nodev 2 2
cases.stdout:
bad-op status=1 err=bad-op
bad-minimum status=1 err=bad-min
bad-maximum status=1 err=bad-max
negative-bound status=1 err=bad-min
bound-over-int-max status=1 err=bad-min
min-greater-than-max status=1 err=min-gt-max
no-device status=2 err=usage
too-many-args status=2 err=usage
add-non-root status=1 err=needs-uid0
delete-non-root status=1 err=needs-uid0
update-non-root status=1 err=needs-uid0
